crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: The analyzed binary is a legitimate instance of the Microsoft Register Server (regsvr32.exe). The decompilation reveals standard functionality for a system utility designed to register and unregister OLE controls, such as DLLs and ActiveX controls, in the Windows Registry. Key behaviors include command-line argument parsing for switches like /s (silent), /u (unregister), and /i (install), followed by the dynamic loading of target libraries using LoadLibraryExW and the invocation of standard exports such as DllRegisterServer, DllUnregisterServer, or DllInstall. The sample also includes logic in TryWow64Scenario to handle cross-architecture registration by re-executing the appropriate version of regsvr32.exe from the System32 or SysWOW64 directories. No malicious redirection or payload execution was identified.
